header.running_head: Making Congregational Du'aa, Raising the Voice and saying 'Aameen'

blocks.text: Kuffaar armies had destroyed. Raising his hands and extending them before his face, Rasulullaah ﷺ cursed the coalition. "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" one of the Bedouins said, "Extend your hands even further." Rasulullaah ﷺ then extended his hands further from his face without raising them higher towards the sky.[^1]
Abu Nu'aym Wahab reports that he saw both Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) pass their hands over their faces after making du'aa.[^2]
Making Congregational Du'aa, Raising the Voice and saying 'Aameen'
Rasulullaah ﷺ Says 'Aameen' to the Du'aas of Hadhrat Zaid (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and another Sahabi (RA)

Hadhrat Qais Madani narrates that when a man came to ask Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) something, he said to the man, "Go to Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) because it once happened that Abu Hurayrah (RA) someone else and I were in the Masjid engaging in Dhikr and making du'aa when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to sit with us. When we fell silent, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked us to continue doing what we had been doing. My companion and I then started making du'aa before Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Rasulullaah ﷺ said 'Aameen' to our du'aas. Abu Hurayrah (RA) then started making du'aa and said, 'O Allaah! I ask You for everything that my two companions have asked for as well as knowledge that I shall never forget.' When Rasulullaah ﷺ said 'Aameen', my companion and I said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! We also ask for knowledge that we shall never forget.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'The man of the Daus tribe (Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)) has beaten you to it.'"[^3]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) makes Du'aa and Requests the People to say 'Aameen' and the Du'aa he made during the 'Year of Ashes'

Hadhrat Jaami bin Shaddaad narrates from a relative that he once heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say, "I want you people to say 'Aameen' to three du'aas that I am going to make." He then proceeded to make du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I am weak so please strengthen me. O Allaah! I am stern, so please soften me. O Allaah! I am miserly so please make me generous."[^4]
Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that it was early one morning during the Year of Ashes (the year in which Madinah experienced a crippling drought) that he saw
Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.291).
Tabraani in his Awsat, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.321).
